provisions.title: Chapter 25 · Congregational Meetings
provisions.body:
BCO 25-1

The congregation consists of all the communing members of a particular church, and they only are entitled to vote.

BCO 25-2

Whenever it may seem for the best interests of the church that a congregational meeting should be held, the Session shall call such meeting and give public notice of at least one week. No business shall be transacted at such meeting except what is stated in the notice. The Session shall always call a congregational meeting when requested in writing to do so: a. by one-fourth (1/4) of the communing members of a church of not more than one hundred (100) such members, b. by one-fifth (1/5) of the communing members of a church of more than one hundred (100) and not more than three hundred (300) such members, c. by one-sixth (1/6) of the communing members of a church of more than three hundred (300) and not more than five hundred (500) such members, d. by one-seventh (1/7) of the communing members of a church of more than five hundred (500) members but not more than seven hundred (700) such members, e. by one hundred (100) of the communing members of a church of more than seven hundred (700) such members. Upon such a proper request, if the Session cannot act, fails to act or refuses to act, to call such a congregational meeting within thirty (30) days from the receipt of such a request, then any member or members in good standing may file a complaint in accordance with the provisions of BCO 43.

BCO 25-3

The quorum of the congregational meeting shall consist of one-fourth (1/4) of the resident communing members, if the church has not more than one hundred (100) such members, and of one-sixth (1/6) of the resident communing members if a church has more than one hundred (100) such members.

BCO 25-4

The pastor shall be the moderator of congregational meetings by virtue of his office. If it should be impracticable or inexpedient for him to preside, or if there is no pastor, the Session shall appoint one of their number to call the meeting to order and to preside until the congregation shall elect their presiding officer, who may be a minister or ruling elder of the Presbyterian Church in America, or any male member of that particular church.

BCO 25-5

A clerk shall be elected by the congregation to serve at that meeting or for a definite period, whose duty shall be to keep correct minutes of the proceedings and of all business transacted and to preserve these minutes in a permanent form, after they have been attested by the moderator and the clerk of the meeting. He shall also send a copy of these minutes to the Session of the church.

BCO 25-6

A particular church which is not incorporated, desiring to elect trustees, may select from among its membership trustees or officers of like nature who shall have the power and authority: a. to buy, sell, or mortgage property for the church, b. to accept and execute deeds as such trustees, c. to hold and defend titles to the same, and d. to manage any permanent special funds entrusted to them for the furtherance of the purposes of the church. In the fulfillment of their duties, such trustees shall be subject always to the authority, and shall act solely under the instructions of the congregation which they serve as trustees. The powers or duties of such trustees must not infringe upon the powers or duties of the Session or of the Board of Deacons. Such trustees shall be elected in regularly constituted congregational meetings.

BCO 25-7

If a particular church is incorporated, the provisions of its charter and bylaws must always be in accord with the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America. All the communing members on the roll of that church shall be members of the corporation. The officers of the corporation, whether they be given the title trustee or some other title, shall be elected from among the members of the corporation in a regularly constituted congregational meeting. The powers and duties of such officers must not infringe upon the powers and duties of the Session or the Board of Deacons. All funds collected for the support and expense of the church and for the benevolent purposes of the church shall be controlled and disbursed by the Session and the Board of Deacons as their relative authorities may from time to time be established and defined. To the officers of the corporation may be given by the charter and bylaws of the corporation any or all of the following responsibilities: a. the buying, selling and mortgaging of property for the church, b. the acquiring and conveying title to such property, the holding and defending title to the same, c. the managing of any permanent special funds entrusted to them for the furtherance of the purposes of the church, provided that such duties do not infringe upon the powers and duties of the Session or of the Board of Deacons. In buying, selling, and mortgaging real property such officers shall act solely under the authority of the corporation, granted in a duly constituted meeting of the corporation.

BCO 25-8

The corporation of a particular church, through its duly elected trustees or corporation officers, (or, if unincorporated, through those who are entitled to represent the particular church in matters related to real property) shall have sole title to its property, real, personal, or mixed, tangible or intangible, and shall be sole owner of any equity in any real estate, or any fund or property of any kind held by or belonging to any particular church, or any board, society, committee, Sunday school class or branch thereof. The superior courts of the Church may receive monies or properties from a local church only by free and voluntary action of the latter.

BCO 25-9

All particular churches shall be entitled to hold, own and enjoy their own local properties, without any right of reversion whatsoever to any Presbytery, General Assembly or any other courts hereafter created, trustees or other officers of such courts.

BCO 25-10

The provisions of this BCO 25 are to be construed as a solemn covenant whereby the Church as a whole promises never to attempt to secure possession of the property of any congregation against its will, whether or not such congregation remains within or chooses to withdraw from this body. All officers and courts of the Church are hereby prohibited from making any such attempt.

BCO 25-11

While a congregation consists of all the communing members of a particular church, and in matters ecclesiastical the actions of such local congregation or church shall be in conformity with the provisions of this Book of Church Order, nevertheless, in matters pertaining to the subject matters referred to in this BCO 25, including specifically the right to affiliate with or become a member of this body or a Presbytery hereof and the right to withdraw from or to sever any affiliation of connection with this body or any Presbytery hereof, action may be taken by such local congregation or local church in accordance with the civil laws applicable to such local congregation or local church; and as long as such action is taken in compliance with such applicable civil laws, then such shall be the action of the local congregation or local church. It is expressly recognized that each local congregation or local church shall be competent to function and to take actions covering the matters set forth herein as long as such action is in compliance with the civil laws with which said local congregation or local church must comply, and this right shall never be taken from said local congregation or local church without the express consent of and affirmative action of such local church or congregation. Particular churches need remain in association with any court of this body only so long as they themselves so desire. The relationship is voluntary, based upon mutual love and confidence, and is in no sense to be maintained by the exercise of any force or coercion whatsoever. A particular church may withdraw from any court of this body at any time for reasons which seem to it sufficient, provided, however, the congregation is given at least thirty-days' notice of any meeting where the congregation is to vote on a proposed withdrawal from the Presbyterian Church in America.

BCO 25-12

If a church is dissolved by the Presbytery at the request of the congregation and no disposition has been made of its property by those who hold the title to the property within six months after such dissolution, then those who held the title to the property at the time of such dissolution shall deliver, convey and transfer to the Presbytery of which the church was a member, or to the authorized agents of the Presbytery, all property of the church; and the receipt and acquittance of the Presbytery, or its proper representatives, shall be a full and complete discharge of all liabilities of such persons holding the property of the church. The Presbytery receiving such property shall apply the same or the proceeds thereof at its discretion.

provisions.title: Section 25-2
provisions.body: Whenever it may seem for the best interests of the church that a congregational meeting should be held, the Session shall call such meeting and give public notice of at least one week. No business shall be transacted at such meeting except what is stated in the notice. The Session shall always call a congregational meeting when requested in writing to do so: a. by one-fourth (1/4) of the communing members of a church of not more than one hundred (100) such members, b. by one-fifth (1/5) of the communing members of a church of more than one hundred (100) and not more than three hundred (300) such members, c. by one-sixth (1/6) of the communing members of a church of more than three hundred (300) and not more than five hundred (500) such members, d. by one-seventh (1/7) of the communing members of a church of more than five hundred (500) members but not more than seven hundred (700) such members, e. by one hundred (100) of the communing members of a church of more than seven hundred (700) such members. Upon such a proper request, if the Session cannot act, fails to act or refuses to act, to call such a congregational meeting within thirty (30) days from the receipt of such a request, then any member or members in good standing may file a complaint in accordance with the provisions of BCO 43.

The SJC held the BCO silent on both points: once the original call and terms are approved, later changes are budgetary and belong to the session under BCO 12-5b; publicizing the budget is prudent but not mandated. metadata.synopsis: The SJC addressed whether a presbytery and its administrative/judicial commission could suspend a local session and assume original jurisdiction over charges against a ruling elder. It answered no: original jurisdiction belonged to the session, and a presbytery cannot "act for" a lower court by replacing congregationally elected elders. Preliminary Principle Six, BCO 16-2, and BCO 31-1/33-1 controlled; the commission's interpretation of BCO 13-9 conflicted with those principles. The Presbytery's and Commission's actions, including the censure approved by Presbytery, were reversed.

It declined to rule on the meeting's legal effect.

provisions.title: Section 25-7
provisions.body: If a particular church is incorporated, the provisions of its charter and bylaws must always be in accord with the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America. All the communing members on the roll of that church shall be members of the corporation. The officers of the corporation, whether they be given the title trustee or some other title, shall be elected from among the members of the corporation in a regularly constituted congregational meeting. The powers and duties of such officers must not infringe upon the powers and duties of the Session or the Board of Deacons. All funds collected for the support and expense of the church and for the benevolent purposes of the church shall be controlled and disbursed by the Session and the Board of Deacons as their relative authorities may from time to time be established and defined. To the officers of the corporation may be given by the charter and bylaws of the corporation any or all of the following responsibilities: a. the buying, selling and mortgaging of property for the church, b. the acquiring and conveying title to such property, the holding and defending title to the same, c. the managing of any permanent special funds entrusted to them for the furtherance of the purposes of the church, provided that such duties do not infringe upon the powers and duties of the Session or of the Board of Deacons. In buying, selling, and mortgaging real property such officers shall act solely under the authority of the corporation, granted in a duly constituted meeting of the corporation.

metadata.synopsis: Complainants challenged a Session plan under which most elders voluntarily resigned, the Session granted severance and benefits to its former pastor, proposed about a year with an interim pastor before a permanent call, and contemplated revising local bylaws. The SJC denied all four items. Any later call still had to follow the BCO without undue delay, and local bylaws had to remain consistent with it.

provisions.title: Section 25-11
provisions.body: While a congregation consists of all the communing members of a particular church, and in matters ecclesiastical the actions of such local congregation or church shall be in conformity with the provisions of this Book of Church Order, nevertheless, in matters pertaining to the subject matters referred to in this BCO 25, including specifically the right to affiliate with or become a member of this body or a Presbytery hereof and the right to withdraw from or to sever any affiliation of connection with this body or any Presbytery hereof, action may be taken by such local congregation or local church in accordance with the civil laws applicable to such local congregation or local church; and as long as such action is taken in compliance with such applicable civil laws, then such shall be the action of the local congregation or local church. It is expressly recognized that each local congregation or local church shall be competent to function and to take actions covering the matters set forth herein as long as such action is in compliance with the civil laws with which said local congregation or local church must comply, and this right shall never be taken from said local congregation or local church without the express consent of and affirmative action of such local church or congregation. Particular churches need remain in association with any court of this body only so long as they themselves so desire. The relationship is voluntary, based upon mutual love and confidence, and is in no sense to be maintained by the exercise of any force or coercion whatsoever. A particular church may withdraw from any court of this body at any time for reasons which seem to it sufficient, provided, however, the congregation is given at least thirty-days' notice of any meeting where the congregation is to vote on a proposed withdrawal from the Presbyterian Church in America.

provisions.title: Section 25-12
provisions.body: If a church is dissolved by the Presbytery at the request of the congregation and no disposition has been made of its property by those who hold the title to the property within six months after such dissolution, then those who held the title to the property at the time of such dissolution shall deliver, convey and transfer to the Presbytery of which the church was a member, or to the authorized agents of the Presbytery, all property of the church; and the receipt and acquittance of the Presbytery, or its proper representatives, shall be a full and complete discharge of all liabilities of such persons holding the property of the church. The Presbytery receiving such property shall apply the same or the proceeds thereof at its discretion.

provisions.title: Chapter 26 · Amending the Constitution of the Church
provisions.body:
BCO 26-1

The Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America, which is subject to and subordinate to the Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments, the inerrant Word of God, consists of its doctrinal standards set forth in the Westminster Confession of Faith, together with the Larger and Shorter Catechisms, and the Book of Church Order, comprising the Form of Government, the Rules of Discipline and the Directory for Worship; all as adopted by the Church.

BCO 26-2

Amendments to the Book of Church Order may be made only in the following manner: 1. Approval of the proposed amendment by majority of those present and voting in the General Assembly, and its recommendation to the Presbyteries. 2. The advice and consent of two-thirds (2/3) of the Presbyteries. 3. The approval and enactment by a subsequent General Assembly by a majority of those present and voting.

BCO 26-3

Amendments to the Confession of Faith and the Larger and Shorter Catechisms may be made only in the following manner: 1. Approval of the proposed amendment by three-fourths (3/4) of those present and voting in the General Assembly, and its recommendation to the Presbyteries. 2. The advice and consent of three-fourths (3/4) of the Presbyteries. 3. The approval and enactment by a subsequent General Assembly by three-fourths (3/4) of those present and voting. This paragraph (BCO 26-3) can be amended only by the same method prescribed for the amendment of the Confession of Faith and Catechisms of the church.

BCO 26-4

In voting upon an amendment to the Constitution of the Presbyterian Church in America, the Presbyteries may not divide the parts of the amendment except as directed by the General Assembly which has recommended its adoption.

BCO 26-5

Full organic union and consolidation of the Presbyterian Church in America with any other ecclesiastical body can be effected only in the following manner: 1. The approval of the proposed union by three-fourths (3/4) of those present and voting in the General Assembly and its recommendation to the Presbyteries. 2. The advice and consent of three-fourths (3/4) of the Presbyteries. 3. The approval and consummation by a subsequent General Assembly by three-fourths (3/4) vote of those present and voting. This paragraph (BCO 26-5) can be amended only by the same method prescribed for the amendment of the Confession of Faith and Catechisms of the church.

BCO 26-6

If by reason of the failure of a number of Presbyteries to act, or to report action, on any proposed amendment to the Standards and the response of the Presbyteries is not satisfactory to the succeeding General Assembly, it may defer action for one year. In that event the General Assembly shall urge the delinquent Presbyteries to report their judgment to the next Assembly, which shall take final action on the proposed amendment.

provisions.title: Chapter 27 · Discipline – Its Nature, Subjects and Ends
provisions.body:
BCO 27-1

Discipline is the exercise of authority given the Church by the Lord Jesus Christ to instruct and guide its members and to promote its purity and welfare. The term has two senses: a. the one referring to the whole government, inspection, training, guardianship and control which the church maintains over its members, its officers and its courts; b. the other a restricted and technical sense, signifying judicial process.

BCO 27-2

All baptized persons, being members of the Church are subject to its discipline and entitled to the benefits thereof.

BCO 27-3

The exercise of discipline is highly important and necessary. In its proper usage discipline maintains: a. the glory of God, b. the purity of His Church, c. the keeping and reclaiming of disobedient sinners. Discipline is for the purpose of godliness (1 Timothy 4:7); therefore, it demands a self-examination under Scripture. Its ends, so far as it involves judicial action, are the rebuke of offenses, the removal of scandal, the vindication of the honor of Christ, the promotion of the purity and general edification of the Church, and the spiritual good of offenders themselves.

BCO 27-4

The power which Christ has given the Church is for building up, and not for destruction. It is to be exercised as under a dispensation of mercy and not of wrath. As in the preaching of the Word the wicked are doctrinally separated from the good, so by discipline the Church authoritatively separates between the holy and the profane. In this it acts the part of a tender mother, correcting her children for their good, that every one of them may be presented faultless in the day of the Lord Jesus. Discipline is systematic training under the authority of God's Scripture. No communing or non-communing member of the Church should be allowed to stray from the Scripture's discipline. Therefore, teaching elders must: a. instruct the officers in discipline, b. instruct the congregation in discipline, c. jointly practice it in the context of the congregation and church courts.

BCO 27-5

Scriptural law is the basis of all discipline because it is the revelation of God's Holy will. Proper disciplinary principles are set forth in the Scriptures and must be followed. They are: a. Instruction in the Word; b. Individual's responsibility to admonish one another (Matthew 18:15, Galatians 6:1); c. If the admonition is rejected, then the calling of one or more witnesses (Matthew 18:16); d. If rejection persists, then the Church must act through her court unto admonition, suspension, excommunication and deposition (See BCO 29 and 30 for further explanation). Steps (a) through (d) must be followed in proper order for the exercise of discipline.

provisions.title: Section 27-4
provisions.body: The power which Christ has given the Church is for building up, and not for destruction. It is to be exercised as under a dispensation of mercy and not of wrath. As in the preaching of the Word the wicked are doctrinally separated from the good, so by discipline the Church authoritatively separates between the holy and the profane. In this it acts the part of a tender mother, correcting her children for their good, that every one of them may be presented faultless in the day of the Lord Jesus. Discipline is systematic training under the authority of God's Scripture. No communing or non-communing member of the Church should be allowed to stray from the Scripture's discipline. Therefore, teaching elders must: a. instruct the officers in discipline, b. instruct the congregation in discipline, c. jointly practice it in the context of the congregation and church courts.

provisions.title: Section 27-5
provisions.body: Scriptural law is the basis of all discipline because it is the revelation of God's Holy will. Proper disciplinary principles are set forth in the Scriptures and must be followed. They are: a. Instruction in the Word; b. Individual's responsibility to admonish one another (Matthew 18:15, Galatians 6:1); c. If the admonition is rejected, then the calling of one or more witnesses (Matthew 18:16); d. If rejection persists, then the Church must act through her court unto admonition, suspension, excommunication and deposition (See BCO 29 and 30 for further explanation). Steps (a) through (d) must be followed in proper order for the exercise of discipline.

provisions.title: Chapter 28 · Disciplining of Non-communing Members
provisions.body:
BCO 28-1

The spiritual nurture, instruction and training of the children of the Church are committed by God primarily to their parents. They are responsible to the Church for the faithful discharge of their obligations. It is a principal duty of the Church to promote true religion in the home. True discipleship involves learning the Word of God under the guidance of the Holy Spirit both at home and in the Church. Without learning there is no growth and without growth there is no discipline and without discipline there is sin and iniquity (1 Timothy 4:7).

BCO 28-2

The home and the Church should also make special provision for instructing the children in the Bible and in the church Catechisms. To this end Sessions should establish and conduct under their authority Sunday schools and Bible classes, and adopt such other methods as may be found helpful. The Session shall encourage the parents of the Church to guide their children in the catechising and disciplining of them in the Christian religion.

BCO 28-3

The Church should maintain constant and sympathetic relations with the children. It also should encourage them, on coming to years of discretion, to make confession of the Lord Jesus Christ and to enter upon all privileges of full church membership. If they are wayward they should be cherished by the church and every means used to reclaim them.

BCO 28-4

Adult non-communing members, who receive with meekness and appreciation the oversight and instruction of the Church, are entitled to special attention. Their rights and privileges under the covenant should be frequently and fully explained, and they should be warned of the sin and danger of neglecting their covenant obligations.

BCO 28-5

All non-communing members shall be deemed under the care of the church to which their parents belong, if they live under the parental roof and are minors; otherwise, under that of the church where they reside, or with which they ordinarily worship.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained Psiaki’s complaint and held that the CPC Session erred by ordaining and installing officers elected at a February 5, 2023 congregational meeting where the congregation’s bylaw excluded communing members under 18 from voting. provisions.title: Chapter 29 · Offenses
provisions.body:
BCO 29-1

An offense, the proper object of judicial process, is anything in the doctrines or practice of a Church member professing faith in Christ which is contrary to the Word of God. The Confession of Faith and the Larger and Shorter Catechisms of the Westminster Assembly, together with the formularies of government, discipline, and worship are accepted by the Presbyterian Church in America as standard expositions of the teachings of Scripture in relation to both faith and practice. Nothing, therefore, ought to be considered by any court as an offense, or admitted as a matter of accusation, which cannot be proved to be such from Scripture.

BCO 29-2

Offenses are either personal or general, private or public; but all of them being sins against God, are therefore grounds of discipline.

BCO 29-3

Personal offenses are violations of the divine law, considered in the special relation of wrongs or injuries to particular individuals. General offenses are heresies or immoralities having no such relation, or considered apart from it.

BCO 29-4

Private offenses are those which are known only to a few persons. Public offenses are those which are notorious.

metadata.synopsis: Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot.

metadata.synopsis: A complainant challenged Nashville Presbytery's handling of allegations against a teaching elder. The SJC held the matter judicially out of order and dismissed it, finding the original filing with the church session was not a BCO 43-1 complaint because the session lacked jurisdiction over the teaching elder. Presbytery properly treated the allegations as BCO 31-2/34-1 reports, and the complainant, not a Nashville member, lacked standing to complain about that new action. A nine-member dissent argued the filing of charges conferred standing under prior SJC cases.

metadata.synopsis: A church member challenged Presbytery’s denial of his complaint after it resolved accusations against a minister through a BCO 38-1 confession rather than trial. The SJC held that using confession without process was not itself error, but the statement and confession failed to correlate with and address the specific allegations. It sustained the complaint, annulled the denial, and remanded for Presbytery to amend the documents, institute process, reactivate the investigative committee, or otherwise respond directly and specifically to the unresolved allegations.

The SJC denied his complaint because Presbytery found that BCO 31-8 applied to Hahn’s conduct and that the evidence did not create a strong presumption of guilt. Deferring to Presbytery absent clear error, the SJC left its refusal to appoint a prosecutor and commence process undisturbed. A concurrence agreed with the result but disputed the majority’s suggestion that filing charges generally requires process.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC denied Hopper's complaint against James River Presbytery's April 13, 1991 order barring him from teaching or preaching his views on prophecy and tongues. It rejected all five specifications: Scripture did not forbid the order; the 1974 Pastoral Letter did not address presbytery's power to enjoin such teaching; forbearance did not preclude protecting peace and purity; presbytery could restrict preaching short of a heresy finding without binding conscience; and allowing presbyteral discussion while restricting congregational teaching was not inconsistent. The action remained in force.

metadata.synopsis: Bowen challenged Presbytery’s attempt, two years after installation, to rescind its earlier ruling and annul local officers’ elections and ordinations without trial. The SJC sustained the complaint: ordination is perpetual, deposition requires judicial process, and rescission was out of order after implementation; Presbytery likewise could not suspend a local elder without due process. The officers remained in office but doctrinally out of accord; voluntary demission or proper process was advised.

provisions.title: Chapter 30 · Church Censures
provisions.body:
BCO 30-1

The censures, which may be inflicted by church courts, are admonition, suspension from the Sacraments, excommunication, suspension from office, and deposition from office. The censures of admonition or definite suspension from office shall be administered to an accused who, upon conviction, satisfies the court as to his repentance and makes such restitution as is appropriate. Such censure concludes the judicial process. The censures of indefinite suspension or excommunication shall be administered to an accused who, upon conviction, remains impenitent.

BCO 30-2

Admonition is the formal reproof of an offender by a church court, warning him of his guilt and danger, and exhorting him to be more circumspect and watchful in the future.

BCO 30-3

Suspension from Sacraments is the temporary exclusion from those ordinances, and is indefinite as to its duration. There is no definite suspension from the Sacraments. Suspension from office is the exclusion of a church officer from his office. This may be definite or indefinite as to its duration. With respect to church officers, suspension from Sacraments shall always be accompanied by suspension from office. But suspension from office is not always necessarily accompanied with suspension from Sacraments. Definite suspension from office is administered when the credit of religion, the honor of Christ, and the good of the delinquent demand it, even though the delinquent has given satisfaction to the court. Indefinite suspension is administered to the impenitent offender until he exhibits signs of repentance, or until by his conduct, the necessity of the greatest censure be made manifest. In the case of indefinite suspension from office imposed due to scandalous conduct, the procedure outlined in BCO 34-8 shall be followed.

BCO 30-4

Excommunication is the excision of an offender from the communion of the Church. This censure is to be inflicted only on account of gross crime or heresy and when the offender shows himself incorrigible and contumacious. The design of this censure is to operate on the offender as a means of reclaiming him, to deliver the church from the scandal of his offense, and to inspire all with fear by the example of his discipline.

BCO 30-5

Deposition is the degradation of an officer from his office, and may or may not be accompanied with the infliction of other censure.

metadata.synopsis: TE Kevin Bigelow complained against multiple actions of North Florida Presbytery related to the dissolution of his call as Assistant Pastor of Christ Church East (where he was also serving as planting pastor at Christ Church Beaches). The SJC sustained the complaint in part (22-0-0), finding that Presbytery erred in ruling four of Bigelow's five complaints out of order; however, after reviewing the substance of all five complaints, the SJC denied each on the merits, concluding Presbytery committed no clear error in dissolving the call, that no congregational vote of CCB was constitutionally required, and that no formal discipline without process had occurred.

relationships.title: Flatgard v. Metro Atlanta Presbytery

The case generated extensive concurring and dissenting opinions debating appellate deference standards under BCO 39-3.2, 39-3.3, and 39-3.4.

The SJC held BCO 32-20 barred Specifications 1, 2, and 4 because Presbytery lacked extraordinary justification for prosecuting old allegations, but did not bar ongoing Specification 3. metadata.synopsis: A teaching elder appealed his judgment and deposition for refusing Presbytery committee directives and allegedly avoiding accountability. The SJC sustained five of nine specifications, holding that the committee could not impose requirements lacking constitutional warrant or control an independent mission board; vague allegations and testimony unavailable for cross-examination also impaired the trial. Because the record did not prove an ongoing pattern of insubordination, it vacated the censure and remanded for a constitutionally compliant proceeding or dismissal. metadata.synopsis: Abshire challenged Presbytery’s commission for its appointment, scope, exhortation, summary disposition of two elders’ complaint, and other actions. The SJC sustained only the challenge to deciding the elders’ complaint without BCO 43 procedures and remanded that complaint. It denied the other issues: the commission could conduct the required investigation, the scope objection was untimely, and its exhortation and report were pastoral rather than formal discipline. relationships.title: Nickoley and Stephens v. Southwest Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Complainants challenged Southwest Presbytery's January 1991 actions: withdrawing charges against two ruling elders, dissolving Pastor Pollock's pastoral relationship, and rescinding its suspension of Covenant PC's session. The SJC did not sustain the complaint and affirmed. It held the BCO gives no presbytery authority to suspend a session or act as a Session pro tem without formal congregational consent; BCO 31-1 left the elder charges with the session, so they were never validly before Presbytery; the dissolution challenge was moot after Pollock left the PCA, though Presbytery acted correctly on the congregation's request.

topics: fundamentals of the system of doctrine
suspension from office without due process
metadata.synopsis: Bowen challenged Presbytery’s attempt, two years after installation, to rescind its earlier ruling and annul local officers’ elections and ordinations without trial. The SJC sustained the complaint: ordination is perpetual, deposition requires judicial process, and rescission was out of order after implementation; Presbytery likewise could not suspend a local elder without due process. But it affirmed that infant baptism and limited atonement are fundamentals admitting no officer exception. The officers remained in office but doctrinally out of accord; voluntary demission or proper process was advised.

relationships.title: Chappell v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery

topics: suspension of session without due process
metadata.synopsis: Ruling Elder Chappell complained against Eastern Carolina Presbytery's Commission, which had suspended the session of Fuller Memorial Presbyterian Church and constituted itself as a 'Session Pro Tem' without due process or congregational consent. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding that the BCO grants no authority for a presbytery to depose a session and act in its place, that suspension requires due process, and that the congregation has an inalienable right to be governed by officers it has chosen.

metadata.synopsis: South Florida Presbytery deposed a Teaching Elder, suspended him from the sacraments, and later excommunicated him without first assigning him to a particular church under BCO 46-8. The complainant argued that omission stripped Presbytery of jurisdiction. The SJC denied the complaint: BCO 46-8 requires assignment but fixes no timeframe or mechanism; a deposed minister remains under Presbytery's jurisdiction until transfer, and BCO 37-9(a) preserves censure authority. Deferring under BCO 39-3, the SJC found no clear error in Presbytery's efforts. Two concurrences agreed in result but disputed the majority's broad reasoning and deference.

metadata.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE John Evans without process after considering investigative-committee observations he had not approved. The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded. BCO 38-1 requires the accused and court to approve one full statement of facts; Evans could not approve facts presented after he left. But the provision does not expressly require a meeting or detailed discussion. The underlying matter remained unresolved: Presbytery could proceed with or without process, or dismiss it.

relationships.title: Fozard v. North Texas Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: At issue was whether North Texas Presbytery wrongly denied a complaint challenging Fort Worth Presbyterian Church’s “Special Case Felons” integration policy as contrary to Scripture. The SJC denied the complaint, holding that the complainant did not show the Session violated Scripture or the Constitution and that BCO 39-3.3 required deference absent clear error, leaving the lower-court actions in effect. The decision, adopted 20-1, expressly did not endorse the Respondents’ Preliminary Principles arguments; a concurrence disclaimed approval of the policy, and one member dissented.

relationships.title: Frazier v. Nashville Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: The SJC denied a complaint challenging Nashville Presbytery's decision not to indict a teaching elder for allegedly sinful teaching on homosexuality and same-sex attraction. The adopted judgment held that the 147-page record showed Presbytery fulfilled its BCO 31-2 investigatory duty and did not show it erred in judgment when it declined process; the complaint was denied 20-0-1. Concurring opinions raised concerns about committee recusal, record clarity, and exegetical uses of Scripture, but they were separate and did not alter the denial.

relationships.title: Bumgarner v. Presbytery of the Mississippi Valley

metadata.synopsis: A claimant sought BCO 40-5 review of Presbytery’s handling of his earlier judicial case, alleging grossly unconstitutional proceedings and delinquency in failing to investigate his 2012 deposition. The SJC found the application administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order because BCO 40-3 excludes judicial-case proceedings from review and control when notice of appeal or complaint has been given, and he had withdrawn his 2012 complaint acknowledging it could not be resubmitted. It dismissed under OMSJC 9.2(d). The concurrence added that BCO 40 cannot refile a withdrawn complaint or reverse a censure.

provisions.title: Section 30-3
provisions.body: Suspension from Sacraments is the temporary exclusion from those ordinances, and is indefinite as to its duration. There is no definite suspension from the Sacraments. Suspension from office is the exclusion of a church officer from his office. This may be definite or indefinite as to its duration. With respect to church officers, suspension from Sacraments shall always be accompanied by suspension from office. But suspension from office is not always necessarily accompanied with suspension from Sacraments. Definite suspension from office is administered when the credit of religion, the honor of Christ, and the good of the delinquent demand it, even though the delinquent has given satisfaction to the court. Indefinite suspension is administered to the impenitent offender until he exhibits signs of repentance, or until by his conduct, the necessity of the greatest censure be made manifest. In the case of indefinite suspension from office imposed due to scandalous conduct, the procedure outlined in BCO 34-8 shall be followed.

metadata.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE John Evans without process after considering investigative-committee observations he had not approved. The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded. BCO 38-1 requires the accused and court to approve one full statement of facts; Evans could not approve facts presented after he left. provisions.title: Chapter 31 · The Parties in Cases of Process
provisions.body:
BCO 31-1

Original jurisdiction (the right first or initially to hear and determine) in relation to ministers of the Gospel shall be in the Presbytery of which the minister is a member, except in cases as provided in BCO 34-1. Such original jurisdiction in relation to church members shall be in the Session of the church of which he/she is a member, except in cases as provided in BCO 33-1.

BCO 31-2

It is the duty of all church Sessions and Presbyteries to exercise care over those subject to their authority. They shall with due diligence and great discretion demand from such persons satisfactory explanations concerning reports affecting their Christian character. This duty is more imperative when those who deem themselves aggrieved by injurious reports shall ask an investigation. If such investigation, however originating, should result in raising a strong presumption of the guilt of the party involved, the court shall institute process, and shall appoint a prosecutor to prepare the indictment and to conduct the case. This prosecutor shall be a member of the court, except that in a case before the Session, he may be any communing member of the same congregation with the accused.

BCO 31-3

The original and only parties in a case of process are the accuser and the accused. The accuser is always the Presbyterian Church in America, whose honor and purity are to be maintained. The prosecutor, whether voluntary or appointed, is always the representative of the Church, and as such has all its rights in the case. In appellate courts the parties are known as appellant and appellee.

BCO 31-4

Every indictment shall begin: "In the name of the Presbyterian Church in America," and shall conclude, "against the peace, unity and purity of the Church, and the honor and majesty of the Lord Jesus Christ, as the King and Head thereof." In every case the Church is the injured and accusing party, against the accused.

BCO 31-5

An injured party shall not become a prosecutor of personal offenses without having tried the means of reconciliation and of reclaiming the offender, required by Christ. "Moreover, if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother but if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established" (Matthew 18:15-16). A church court, however, may judicially investigate personal offenses as if general when the interest of religion seem to demand it. So, also, those to whom private offenses are known cannot become prosecutors without having previously endeavored to remove the scandal by private means.

BCO 31-6

When the offense is general, the case may be conducted either by any person appearing as prosecutor or by a prosecutor appointed by the court.

BCO 31-7

When the prosecution is instituted by the court, the previous steps required by our Lord in the case of personal offenses are not necessary. There are many cases, however, in which it will promote the interests of religion to send a committee to converse in a private manner with the offender, and endeavor to bring him to a sense of his guilt, before instituting actual process.

BCO 31-8

Great caution ought to be exercised in receiving accusations from any person who is known to indulge a malignant spirit towards the accused; who is not of good character; who is himself under censure or process; who is deeply interested in any respect in the conviction of the accused; or who is known to be litigious, rash or highly imprudent.

BCO 31-9

Every voluntary prosecutor shall be previously warned, that if he fail to show probable cause of the charges, he may himself be censured as a slanderer of the brethren.

BCO 31-10

When a member of a church court is under process, all his official functions may be administratively suspended at the court's discretion; but this shall never be done in the way of censure, and this requires a two-thirds (2/3) majority of members present and voting (not counting abstentions) at the meeting of the Session or Presbytery, even if the process is being conducted by a commission.

BCO 31-11

In the discussion of all questions arising in his own case, the accused shall exercise the rights of defendant only, not of judge.

relationships.title: Session of First Presbyterian Church North Port v. Presbytery of Southwest Florida

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained the Session's complaint against Presbytery. Presbytery had ruled a member's original complaint administratively out of order as untimely but then remanded the matter to the Session; the SJC held that once out of order, no complaint remained to remand. It also held Presbytery could not direct or instruct the Session to initiate formal process without BCO 40-5's required citation step, so those directions were null and void. The member remained under the Session's jurisdiction; the civil trespass order was not ecclesiastical discipline and did not alter membership.

relationships.title: Brown v. Northern California Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Brown challenged Presbytery’s abstract approval of six views concerning diaconal practice. The SJC sustained the consolidated complaints and annulled Presbytery’s action because a church court cannot issue a binding decree apart from properly exercising jurisdiction over specific persons. Constitutional conformity must instead be determined through authorized examination or judicial processes. The judgment deliberately left unresolved whether any of the six views themselves were faithful to the Constitution; the detailed view-by-view analysis appeared only in a concurring opinion.

provisions.title: Section 31-2
provisions.body: It is the duty of all church Sessions and Presbyteries to exercise care over those subject to their authority. They shall with due diligence and great discretion demand from such persons satisfactory explanations concerning reports affecting their Christian character. This duty is more imperative when those who deem themselves aggrieved by injurious reports shall ask an investigation. If such investigation, however originating, should result in raising a strong presumption of the guilt of the party involved, the court shall institute process, and shall appoint a prosecutor to prepare the indictment and to conduct the case. This prosecutor shall be a member of the court, except that in a case before the Session, he may be any communing member of the same congregation with the accused.

The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained a session's timely complaint that Louisiana Presbytery barred one of its members from the Lord's Table after assuming original jurisdiction. Under BCO 33-1, a presbytery may assume jurisdiction only when the session 'refuses to act'; because the session had investigated and found no strong presumption of guilt, it acted, so LAP never acquired jurisdiction. provisions.title: Section 31-3
provisions.body: The original and only parties in a case of process are the accuser and the accused. The accuser is always the Presbyterian Church in America, whose honor and purity are to be maintained. The prosecutor, whether voluntary or appointed, is always the representative of the Church, and as such has all its rights in the case. In appellate courts the parties are known as appellant and appellee.

The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s action because discipline preceded particular charges and a specific confession, and because an independent church lacked authority to impose PCA censure. The SJC left guilt intact and denied a new trial, though it held that a prosecutor may not deliberate as a judge. metadata.synopsis: Smith appealed discipline for divisiveness, gossip and slander, broken membership vows, and contumacy arising largely from complaints and letters during church conflict. The SJC sustained her appeal, reversed guilt on all four charges, and annulled suspension from the sacraments. The SJC declined remand because the evidence was insufficient.

provisions.title: Section 31-5
provisions.body: An injured party shall not become a prosecutor of personal offenses without having tried the means of reconciliation and of reclaiming the offender, required by Christ. "Moreover, if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother but if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established" (Matthew 18:15-16). A church court, however, may judicially investigate personal offenses as if general when the interest of religion seem to demand it. So, also, those to whom private offenses are known cannot become prosecutors without having previously endeavored to remove the scandal by private means.

The complaint challenged a Session's reception of and action on a confession at a meeting more than six months before filing, far outside BCO 43-2's sixty-day period; the SJC held the untimeliness was not demonstrated curable. metadata.synopsis: South Florida Presbytery deposed a Teaching Elder, suspended him from the sacraments, and later excommunicated him without first assigning him to a particular church under BCO 46-8. The complainant argued that omission stripped Presbytery of jurisdiction. The SJC denied the complaint: BCO 46-8 requires assignment but fixes no timeframe or mechanism; a deposed minister remains under Presbytery's jurisdiction until transfer, and BCO 37-9(a) preserves censure authority. Deferring under BCO 39-3, the SJC found no clear error in Presbytery's efforts. Two concurrences agreed in result but disputed the majority's broad reasoning and deference.

metadata.synopsis: TE Sam Jung Suh appealed his indefinite suspension by Korean Southeastern Presbytery following a trial on charges of financial misconduct. The SJC reversed the conviction in whole, finding that the pre-investigative and BCO 31-2 investigation phases were marred by grave constitutional errors including failure to comply with BCO 27-5, failure to demand satisfactory explanations from TE Suh, improper expansion of the investigation, and absence of a valid antecedent condition necessary to institute process; multiple dissents argued the SJC should have deferred to the lower court's factual findings and trial verdict.

The decision was adopted 23-0 on a roll call, one absent, on the officers' recommendation. The record does not identify the underlying presbytery action or reach the complaint's merits, so the case's value is its threshold standing ruling, not any complaint determination.

metadata.synopsis: A ruling elder appealed convictions for distributing an SJC decision contrary to Session's will and for allegedly false, divisive statements in an email opposing a pastoral-election proposal. The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed Session and Presbytery in whole, rendered not guilty, removed the indefinite suspension, and restored him to office. Session could not bind conscience without scriptural authority, and no express prohibition or proof of falsity existed. Many other specifications were rejected; a concurrence cautioned that such emails are rarely wise.

metadata.synopsis: A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination 'vetting' removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1's sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session's sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.

metadata.synopsis: Grace PCA’s Session challenged Ohio Presbytery’s reversal of excommunication for two members convicted of heresy. The SJC partially sustained the complaint: prior indefinite suspension was not constitutionally required, but Presbytery properly found excommunication too severe because the trial record contained no evidence of contumacy. Presbytery nevertheless had to impose an appropriate lesser censure or remand for one, and lacked authority to mandate transfer to another church. The unappealed heresy convictions remained, but because the members had joined another church, further proceedings were moot.

metadata.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE John Evans without process after considering investigative-committee observations he had not approved. The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded. BCO 38-1 requires the accused and court to approve one full statement of facts; Evans could not approve facts presented after he left. But the provision does not expressly require a meeting or detailed discussion. The underlying matter remained unresolved: Presbytery could proceed with or without process, or dismiss it.

metadata.synopsis: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s commissions and its response to a canceled congregational meeting. The SJC upheld the Inman Commission because a Session may reference limited duties without congregational consent. It sustained the challenges to Presbytery’s consideration of the August 7 meeting and appointment of the Sealy Commission because the Session majority had validly canceled the meeting. Linton’s and Pellom’s calls therefore remained undissolved and Neville was uncalled, absent later congregational action. The SJC also upheld Presbytery’s criticism of the cancellation as unwise and its refusal to issue a BCO 40-5 citation.

relationships.title: White v. Siouxlands Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: A minister complained that his presbytery wrongly refused to order a BCO 31-2 investigation into another minister’s Covenant of Works/Federal Vision views. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded for that investigation, holding that BCO 31-2 requires investigation of credible, injurious reports about Christian character. The presbytery erred by applying the higher evidentiary standard for conviction after process; reports sufficient to trigger investigation need not establish guilt or a strong presumption of guilt, and hearsay or conflicting testimony can require investigation rather than justify refusal. A concurrence agreed in result; the dissent found no clear error in the presbytery’s exercise of discretion.

It remanded only to impose indefinite suspension from the Sacraments and conditions pending satisfactory evidence of repentance.

metadata.synopsis: An appeal from a Presbytery judgment and indefinite suspension of a pastor turned on whether he violated the Ninth Commandment and ordination/installation vows by telling the congregation the Session had 'demanded' his resignation for six weeks. The SJC denied the appeal, holding the Session as a whole had not formally demanded resignation; individual elders' earlier opinions did not excuse the overstatement, which harmed the Session's good name. It also found no due-process irregularity or prejudice warranting reversal, deferring to the lower court under BCO 39-3, leaving indefinite suspension in place.

The SJC upheld Presbytery's action. It concluded that the record showed no unconstitutional procedure or BCO violation and that it could consider only facts properly in the record, not material from earlier cases offered in oral argument. The ruling left the later membership removal undisturbed.

metadata.synopsis: Brown challenged Presbytery’s abstract approval of six views concerning diaconal practice. The SJC sustained the consolidated complaints and annulled Presbytery’s action because a church court cannot issue a binding decree apart from properly exercising jurisdiction over specific persons. The SJC sustained the complaint and remanded for that investigation, holding that BCO 31-2 requires investigation of credible, injurious reports about Christian character. The presbytery erred by applying the higher evidentiary standard for conviction after process; reports sufficient to trigger investigation need not establish guilt or a strong presumption of guilt, and hearsay or conflicting testimony can require investigation rather than justify refusal. A concurrence agreed in result; the dissent found no clear error in the presbytery’s exercise of discretion.

provisions.title: Chapter 32 · General Provisions Applicable to all Cases of Process
provisions.body:
BCO 32-1

It is incumbent on every member of a court of Jesus Christ engaged in a trial of offenders, to bear in mind the inspired injunction: "Brethren, if a man is overtaken in any trespass, you who are spiritual restore such a one in the spirit of gentleness, considering yourself lest you also be tempted" (Galatians 6:1).

BCO 32-2

Process against an offender shall not be commenced unless some person or persons undertake to make out the charge; or unless the court finds it necessary, for the honor of religion, itself to take the step provided for in BCO 31-2.

BCO 32-3

It is appropriate that with each citation the moderator or clerk call the attention of the parties to the Rules of Discipline (BCO 27 through 46) and assist the parties to obtain access to them. When a charge is laid before the Session or Presbytery, it shall be reduced to writing, and nothing shall be done at the first meeting of the court, unless by consent of parties, except: 1. to appoint a prosecutor, 2. to order the indictment drawn and a copy, along with names of witnesses then known to support it, served on the accused, and 3. to cite the accused to appear and be heard at another meeting which shall not be sooner than ten days after such citation. At the second meeting of the court the charges shall be read to the accused, if present, and he shall be called upon to say whether he be guilty or not. If the accused confesses, the court may deal with him according to its discretion; if he plead and take issue, the trial shall be scheduled and all parties and their witnesses cited to appear. The trial shall not be sooner than fourteen (14) days after such citation. Accused parties may plead in writing when they cannot be personally present. Parties necessarily absent should have counsel assigned to them.

BCO 32-4

The citation shall be issued and signed by the moderator or clerk by order and in the name of the court. He shall also issue citations to such witnesses as either party shall nominate to appear on his behalf. Indictments and citations shall be delivered in person or in another manner providing verification of the date of receipt. Compliance with these requirements shall be deemed to have been fulfilled if a party cannot be located after diligent inquiry or if a party refuses to accept delivery.

BCO 32-5

In drawing the indictment, the times, places and circumstances should, if possible, be particularly stated, that the accused may have an opportunity to make his defense.

BCO 32-6

a. When an accused person shall refuse to obey a citation, he shall be cited a second time. This second citation shall be accompanied with a notice that if he does not appear at the time appointed (unless providentially hindered, which fact he must make known to the court) he shall be dealt with for his contumacy (cf. BCO 33-2; 34-4). b. When an accused person shall appear and refuse to plead, or otherwise refuse to cooperate with lawful proceedings, he shall be dealt with for his contumacy (cf. BCO 33-2; 34-4).

BCO 32-7

The time which must elapse between the serving of the first citation on the accused person, and the meeting of the court at which he is to appear, shall be at least ten (10) days. The time allotted for his appearance on the subsequent citation shall be left to the discretion of the court, provided that it be quite sufficient for a seasonable and convenient compliance with the citation.

BCO 32-8

When the offense with which an accused person stands charged took place at a distance, and it is inconvenient for the witnesses to appear before the court having jurisdiction, that court may either (a) appoint a commission of its body, or (b) request the coordinate court contiguous to the place where the facts occurred to take the testimony for it, or (c) have the testimony taken by videoconference, which shall employ technical means that ensure that all persons participating in the meeting can see and hear each other at the same time, and which allows for live cross-examination by both parties. The accused shall always have reasonable notice of the time and place of the meeting of this commission or coordinate court.

BCO 32-9

When an offense, alleged to have been committed at a distance, is not likely otherwise to become known to the court having jurisdiction, it shall be the duty of the court within whose bounds the facts occurred, after satisfying itself that there is probable ground for accusation, to send notice to the court having jurisdiction, which shall at once proceed against the accused; or the whole case may be remitted for trial to the coordinate court within whose bounds the offense is alleged to have been committed.

BCO 32-10

Before proceeding to trial, courts ought to ascertain that their citations have been duly served.

BCO 32-11

In every process, if deemed expedient there may be a committee appointed, which shall be called the Judicial Committee, and whose duty it shall be to digest and arrange all the papers, and to prescribe, under the direction of the court, the whole order of the proceedings. The members of this committee shall be entitled, notwithstanding their performance of this duty, to sit and vote in the case as members of the court.

BCO 32-12

When the trial is about to begin, it shall be the duty of the moderator solemnly to announce from the chair that the court is about to pass to the consideration of the case, and to enjoin on the members to recollect and regard their high character as judges of a court of Jesus Christ, and the solemn duty in which they are about to engage.

BCO 32-13

In order that the trial may be fair and impartial, the witnesses shall be examined in the presence of the accused (as permitted by BCO 32-8), or at least after he shall have received due citation to attend. Witnesses may be cross-examined by both parties, and any questions asked must be pertinent to the issue.

BCO 32-14

On all questions arising in the progress of a trial, the discussion shall first be between the parties; and when they have been heard, they may be required to withdraw from the court until the members deliberate upon and decide the point.

BCO 32-15

When a court of first resort proceeds to the trial of a case, the following order shall be observed: 1. The moderator shall charge the court. 2. The indictment shall be read, and the answer of the accused heard. 3. The witnesses for the prosecutor and then those for the accused shall be examined. 4. The parties shall be heard: first, the prosecutor, and then the accused, and the prosecutor shall close. 5. The roll shall be called, and the members may express their opinion in the case. 6. The vote shall be taken, the verdict announced and judgment entered on the records.

BCO 32-16

Either party may, for cause, challenge the right of any member to sit in the trial of the case, which question shall be decided by the other members of the court.

BCO 32-17

Pending the trial of a case, any member of the court who shall express his opinion of its merits to either party, or to any person not a member of the court; or who shall absent himself from any sitting without the permission of the court, or satisfactory reasons rendered, shall be thereby disqualified from taking part in the subsequent proceedings.

BCO 32-18

Minutes of the trial shall be kept by the clerk, which shall exhibit the charges, the answer, record of the testimony, as defined by BCO 35-9, and all such acts, orders, and decisions of the court relating to the case, as either party may desire, and also the judgment. The clerk shall without delay assemble the Record of the Case which shall consist of the charges, the answer, the citations and returns thereto, and the minutes herein required to be kept. The parties shall be allowed copies of the Record of the Case at their own expense if they demand them. When a case is removed by appeal or complaint, the lower court shall transmit "the Record" thus prepared to the higher court with the addition of the notice of appeal or complaint, and the reasons therefor, if any shall have been filed. Nothing which is not contained in this "Record" shall be taken into consideration by the higher court. On the final decision of a case in a higher court, the judgment shall be sent down to the court in which the case originated.

BCO 32-19

No professional counsel shall be permitted as such to appear and plead in cases of process in any court; but an accused person may, if he desires it, be represented before the Session or the Presbytery by any member in good standing of a church in the same Presbytery or by any Teaching Elder member of that Presbytery, or before the General Assembly by any member in good standing in the PCA. A member of the court so employed shall not be allowed to sit in judgment in the case. Courts are encouraged to suggest to the accused/appellant the names of potential representatives and potential advisors he might contact.

BCO 32-20

The accused or a member of the court may object to the consideration of a charge, for example, if he thinks the passage of time since the alleged offense makes fair adjudication unachievable. The court should consider factors such as the gravity of the alleged offense as well as what degradations of evidence and memory may have occurred in the intervening period.

metadata.synopsis: RE Harris, as a Presbytery prosecutor, complained that Wisconsin Presbytery's Judicial Commission erred in dismissing both indictments against a pastor for alleged pastoral care failures. The SJC denied the complaint 18-4-0, finding the JC's dismissal of Indictment 1 under BCO 32-20 (passage of time) was within its discretion despite noting some troubling reasoning by JC members, and that the dismissal of Indictment 2 was authorized because the charge arose from a private offense never brought through proper process; four members dissented as to Indictment 1, arguing the JC clearly erred by conducting a de facto trial with only the accused's unsworn testimony.

The SJC upheld Presbytery's authority to receive credible reports and investigate, but annulled the findings of guilt, censures, and corrective mandates because BCO 40-6 required formal process or an admission before censure. It returned the matter for records review, informal resolution, or formal process and declined interim mandates that would assume the disputed allegations were true.

It held that Presbytery erred when its Judicial Commission found a strong presumption of guilt but, instead of instituting process under BCO 31-2, directed pastoral reconciliation and conditioned later process on its success; that motion also impaired the accused's right against self-incrimination. It further held that BCO 32-20's one-year time bar had run and that the 2022 amendment did not apply retroactively, so Presbytery is debarred from prosecuting the allegations. Four commissioners dissented, disputing the BCO 32-20 ruling.

The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded. metadata.synopsis: An indicted teaching elder challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s approval of a PJC judgment and indefinite suspension after the PJC blended a BCO 32 case of process with a BCO 38-1 case without process. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval, and returned the matter to the PJC. Because he admitted only some indicted charges, his negotiated confession could not satisfy BCO 38-1 and the conversion prejudiced his rights. The PJC may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32; the ruling does not decide whether conversion is ever permissible.

relationships.title: Reese and Bech v. Philadelphia Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Philadelphia Presbytery declared Reese and Bech's complaint out of order because some supporting reasons and requested amends allegedly violated the BCO. The SJC sustained the complaint, holding Presbytery misapplied Robert's Rules: objectionable parts do not justify rejecting an entire complaint, and a court need not adopt requested amends. It also said pertinent questions about whether a call is for the good of the Church may be asked, but agreed the amends—including removing TE Hsu—were inappropriate and could not rescind his installation.

metadata.synopsis: Korean Eastern Presbytery dismissed TE Eliot Lee's charges against two teaching elders without trial, and the SJC sustained Lee's complaint that this was unconstitutional. Although a presbytery may dismiss charges under BCO 29-1, 32-20, 34-2, or 31-8, it bears the burden of documenting that basis; KEP did not. The SJC refused Lee's request that it enter the guilt verdicts the presbytery should have reached—that power exists on appeal, not complaint. It remanded for KEP to begin process under BCO 32.

The SJC sustained the appeal, reversed Session and Presbytery in whole, rendered not guilty, removed the indefinite suspension, and restored him to office. metadata.synopsis: Ryan Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its refusal to commence process against Greg Johnson on four allegations concerning same-sex attraction as sin, identity in Christ, sanctification, and fitness for office. The SJC denied the complaint in full. It found no clear procedural error and held that Johnson’s explanations and clarifications made Presbytery’s non-indictment judgments reasonable. No trial was ordered. The ruling neither adjudged Johnson guilty nor endorsed every statement or broader constitutional position concerning same-sex attraction.

The ruling reserved the session's sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.

metadata.synopsis: Two consolidated complaints challenged Philadelphia Presbytery’s licensing and ordination of a candidate who believed Scripture could permit women to hold the deacon’s office but promised to follow the BCO and not ordain women. The SJC denied both complaints and affirmed Presbytery. It distinguished subscription to doctrinal standards from approval of BCO practices, applied a three-part inquiry, and deferred to Presbytery on the candidate’s credible vow. Because complainants identified no violated doctrinal standard, no error was shown. The ruling reaffirmed that the BCO bars ordaining women as deacons.

provisions.title: Section 32-3
provisions.body: It is appropriate that with each citation the moderator or clerk call the attention of the parties to the Rules of Discipline (BCO 27 through 46) and assist the parties to obtain access to them. When a charge is laid before the Session or Presbytery, it shall be reduced to writing, and nothing shall be done at the first meeting of the court, unless by consent of parties, except: 1. to appoint a prosecutor, 2. to order the indictment drawn and a copy, along with names of witnesses then known to support it, served on the accused, and 3. to cite the accused to appear and be heard at another meeting which shall not be sooner than ten days after such citation. At the second meeting of the court the charges shall be read to the accused, if present, and he shall be called upon to say whether he be guilty or not. If the accused confesses, the court may deal with him according to its discretion; if he plead and take issue, the trial shall be scheduled and all parties and their witnesses cited to appear. The trial shall not be sooner than fourteen (14) days after such citation. Accused parties may plead in writing when they cannot be personally present. Parties necessarily absent should have counsel assigned to them.

metadata.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery divested a minister without censure for prolonged lack of call after he had joined an EPCEW congregation and notified Presbytery of his withdrawal. The SJC sustained his appeal and reversed the divestiture because BCO 38-3(a) had already ended Presbytery's jurisdiction while he was in good standing and under no investigation or charges. It directed Presbytery to record the irregular withdrawal, acknowledge his new membership, and remove him from its roll.

metadata.synopsis: An elder appealed Presbytery’s elevation, without additional process, of suspensions from office and the Sacraments to deposition and excommunication. The SJC granted the appeal, reversed in whole, and remanded, restoring the prior suspensions. Elevation required a hearing on incorrigibility and contumacy—with a charge, evidence, plea, and defense—but not a full de novo trial; disagreement with the original verdict alone was insufficient. The SJC left unresolved deposition from office when excommunication is absent.

relationships.title: Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: The SJC declared Benyola's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order, because Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and thus lacked standing. The decision was adopted 23-0 on a roll call, one absent, on the officers' recommendation. The record does not identify the underlying presbytery action or reach the complaint's merits, so the case's value is its threshold standing ruling, not any complaint determination.

relationships.title: Harrell et al. v. Covenant Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: The SJC sustained an appeal by seven members of a 38-member mission church who were convicted by their temporary Session of opposing the organizing minister's expected election as pastor. Reversing the Presbytery's affirmance and the guilty verdicts underlying indefinite suspensions, the SJC held the indictments fatally lacked BCO 32-5 specificity; Presbytery used the wrong standard of review; the Session had no authority to control pastoral selection; and no Fifth or Ninth Commandment offense was proved. Challenges to witness-judges, venue, and refusal to refer were rejected.

relationships.title: Crouse v. Northwest Georgia Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: A serving deacon nominated for ruling elder complained that his session removed his nomination before BCO 24-1 instruction or examination. The SJC held the session erred by adding an unwritten pre-examination 'vetting' removal and that Northwest Georgia Presbytery erred in approving it: BCO 24-1's sequence—instruction and examination before the session determines eligibility—is mandatory. The ruling reserved the session's sound discretion and the treatment of frivolous or clearly disqualified nominees. The complaint was sustained and remanded for adjudication consistent with the decision.

relationships.title: Evans and Pitts et al. v. Arizona Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: Arizona Presbytery deposed TE John Evans without process after considering investigative-committee observations he had not approved. The SJC sustained the joined complaints, annulled the deposition, and remanded. BCO 38-1 requires the accused and court to approve one full statement of facts; Evans could not approve facts presented after he left. But the provision does not expressly require a meeting or detailed discussion. The underlying matter remained unresolved: Presbytery could proceed with or without process, or dismiss it.

topics: case of process vs case without process
metadata.synopsis: An indicted teaching elder challenged Chesapeake Presbytery’s approval of a PJC judgment and indefinite suspension after the PJC blended a BCO 32 case of process with a BCO 38-1 case without process. The SJC sustained the complaint, annulled Presbytery’s approval, and returned the matter to the PJC. Because he admitted only some indicted charges, his negotiated confession could not satisfy BCO 38-1 and the conversion prejudiced his rights. The PJC may dismiss or proceed under BCO 32; the ruling does not decide whether conversion is ever permissible.

relationships.title: Doty v. Nashville Presbytery

metadata.synopsis: A complainant challenged Nashville Presbytery's handling of allegations against a teaching elder. The SJC held the matter judicially out of order and dismissed it, finding the original filing with the church session was not a BCO 43-1 complaint because the session lacked jurisdiction over the teaching elder. Presbytery properly treated the allegations as BCO 31-2/34-1 reports, and the complainant, not a Nashville member, lacked standing to complain about that new action. A nine-member dissent argued the filing of charges conferred standing under prior SJC cases.
